title: fix(scorers): use structured data boundaries in LLM judge prompts
contribution: Submitted the split a maintainer-filed issue (#62) asked for: trusted grading rules and the text under evaluation occupy separate halves of every LLM-judge prompt. Rules stay in the system message; row values travel as one JSON object in the user message through a single shared helper.
whyItMatters: Row text formatted like a section of the grading instructions can be read by the judge as a peer-level instruction. Separating the two halves narrows that surface; it is not a claim that prompt injection is solved.

title: Structured data boundaries for 12 LLM-judge scorers
contribution: Merged upstream. All 12 scorers in scope (7 Judge classes plus 5 specialized scorers) route through one message builder, evaluated row values no longer enter prompt text at any code path, and a judge whose rule section is missing or blank raises instead of grading without rules. Added 73 offline test cases across 22 test functions.
whyItMatters: Turns an authoring convention into an enforced boundary with regression coverage, and fails loudly where a scorer would otherwise silently grade with no rules.

title: fix(tests): preserve LF bytes in hashed replay fixtures
contribution: Located and diagnosed this while #114 was under review: two write_text() calls hashed LF bytes while Windows wrote CRLF, so seven replay tests failed at the checksum before reaching the assertion they existed to make. The maintainer opened #115 and fixed it in a direct commit.
whyItMatters: A byte-boundary difference in test setup can mask the very validation a suite is supposed to perform. This entry records the diagnosis; the fix is the maintainer's.

title: Failure Attribution and Evaluation Reliability Framework for LongMemEval (methodology report)
contribution: Published the methods half of the Boundary Labs collaboration as its own Zenodo deposit (v2.0 RC3, sole-authored): the four-axis failure-attribution rubric, the T1-T5 diagnostic test matrix with interpretation rules, and the four-rater judging protocol. The joint preprint carries the reconstruction, the rerun and the scores.
whyItMatters: Readers can examine the instrument and its claim boundaries without the run narrative. The report marks figures it did not recompute as collaborator-reported.

title: Infit and outfit statistics return NaN for items with masked missing responses
contribution: Reported, with a CPU reproduction, that infit_statistics() and outfit_statistics() multiply residuals by the response mask, and NaN times zero is still NaN: a masked or absent response propagates through the sum and empties the item statistic instead of being excluded from it.
whyItMatters: Where responses are simply missing, the fit statistic that is supposed to describe a sparse panel disappears with them, so the diagnostic fails on the data it exists to measure.

title: Fix masked NaN in infit and outfit item statistics
contribution: Submitted the narrow fix for #52: torch.where(mask, x, 0.0) replaces the multiply-by-mask in the infit numerator and variance denominator and in the outfit numerator, with four deterministic regression tests. Two files, +33/-3. Open and unreviewed at the last check; no maintainer response yet.
whyItMatters: Keeps the bug report and the proposed repair public and separately dated, so an unmerged fix is never presented as upstream behaviour.

title: Preserve SkillBank state across checkpoint resume
contribution: Submitted a checkpoint-resume fix that saves and restores the training SkillBank, with checkpoint-state validation, atomic writes, and legacy-checkpoint compatibility.
whyItMatters: Prevents a resumed policy from being paired with a SkillBank that never co-evolved with it.

title: Add claude-api Files upload regression example
contribution: Added a Claude API file-upload regression example with failure reproduction, repair steps, and verification.
whyItMatters: Makes an API integration failure reproducible before evaluating a repair.

title: examples: add skill-creator description auth regression case
contribution: Submitted a skill-creator description authorization regression case and repair workflow.
whyItMatters: Tests whether a repair preserves the intended authorization boundary.

title: feat(examples): add Claude API model-retirement repair example
contribution: Submitted a Claude API model-retirement repair example with regression checks.
whyItMatters: Makes a stale API assumption and its repair independently inspectable.

title: fix(harness): wait for steps triggered by passing reports
contribution: Submitted runner lifecycle fixes, regression coverage, and tutorial corrections for passing reports.
whyItMatters: Separates completed evolution steps from whether a new harness head is published.

title: [Bug] Wait for steps triggered by passing reports in the evolve-your-harness runner
contribution: Reported that passing scored reports trigger evolution steps that the tutorial runner did not wait for.
whyItMatters: Identifies a mismatch between submitted feedback and runner completion.

title: update-triage: distinguish missing feedback from GitHub API failures
contribution: Used mocked API failures to show that failed feedback retrieval can look like a successful empty response.
whyItMatters: Missing feedback and unavailable feedback support different conclusions. The reply is automated triage, not human maintainer confirmation.

title: Feedback edits and deletes leave stale few-shot vectors active
contribution: Reproduced stale few-shot evaluator feedback remaining active after feedback edits and deletion.
whyItMatters: Checks whether persistent evaluator state follows the source feedback lifecycle.

title: Review approval survives normal session completion and admits unreviewed final evidence
contribution: Reproduced session approval remaining valid after normal completion adds previously unreviewed final evidence.
whyItMatters: Tests what evidence an approval actually authorizes for downstream training.

title: Update API accepts content changes without re-embedding while docs present content mutation as supported
contribution: Reported API and documentation mismatches around content mutation without re-embedding.
whyItMatters: Clarifies the public mutation contract around an already documented semantic-state constraint.

title: profile.brief and profile.get bypass approval gating for learned preferences
contribution: Reproduced learned preferences crossing the approval gate through profile.brief and profile.get.
whyItMatters: Checks whether serving paths enforce the same learned-preference approval boundary.

title: Suggestions for improving GPTCoach’s reproducibility, privacy compliance, and real-world usability
contribution: Submitted suggestions on reproducibility, privacy compliance, and real-world usability.
whyItMatters: Makes implementation and deployment questions available for public discussion.

title: fix(harness): wait for steps triggered by passing reports
contribution: Fixed runner lifecycle handling, added regression coverage, and corrected tutorial wording; merged upstream.
whyItMatters: Separates completed evolution steps from whether a new harness head is published.

title: [Bug] Wait for steps triggered by passing reports in the evolve-your-harness runner
contribution: Issue #663 was closed after PR #677 merged the runner fix.
whyItMatters: Keeps issue closure dated separately from both the report and merge.

title: Is `recall_used_count` intended to mean verified use or caller-reported use?
contribution: Asked whether the recall-use signal means independently verified use or caller-reported attribution.
whyItMatters: Asks whether a signal affecting future memory ranking represents verified or caller-reported use.

title: Evaluating how feedback reliability shapes future agent behavior
contribution: Proposed a bounded evaluation varying feedback reliability and consistency, with later-task outcomes.
whyItMatters: Provides a public evaluation proposal; no pilot or experiment is claimed.

title: What the Score Measured: Failure Attribution in an Agent Memory Evaluation
contribution: Co-authored a public preprint on failure attribution and evaluation observability with Dino Vitale.
whyItMatters: Documents why outcome scores alone cannot identify which memory-evaluation component failed.

title: Causal Estimation Diagnostics v1.0.0
contribution: Released a CPU-based diagnostic artifact comparing estimator errors and causal-support diagnostics across four frozen regimes.
whyItMatters: Makes diagnostic limits and reproduction evidence inspectable without claiming a new estimator or reliability guarantee.

title: Preference Modeling Diagnostics public snapshot
contribution: Published a frozen CPU-only preference-modeling study with prompt-disjoint evaluation and identity controls.
whyItMatters: Tests a small held-out known-user adaptation benefit while preserving its scope and negative controls.

title: Evaluation Runtime public snapshot
contribution: Specified and co-designed attempt identity, ambiguity-aware recovery, and inspectable report denominators; directed implementation and reviewed checks.
whyItMatters: Provides bounded engineering evidence using deterministic mocks, with no real-provider reliability validation.

title: InteractionKit v1.0.0
contribution: Released typed specifications, composition checks, derived schemas, and self-describing behavioral logs for AI interaction experiments.
whyItMatters: Supports software contract inspection; construct validity and cross-implementation equivalence remain unestablished.

title: CheckMyCoach v2.2-frozen execution package
contribution: Tagged a frozen execution package for the CheckMyCoach evaluation prototype.
whyItMatters: Preserves a versioned software checkpoint; historical heuristic fields are not validated calibration measures.

source.sourceTitle: CheckMyCoach Evaluation v2.2 frozen execution package

title: Validate reward graphs before loading models
contribution: UniRL trains models with configurable reward backends. Submitted a two-phase reward lifecycle: construct and validate the complete graph, then explicitly load models; composite backends forward the load hook. The PR reports CPU-only RED/GREEN checks through both the Worker and Hydra construction paths.
whyItMatters: Invalid reward configurations should fail before checkpoint reads or GPU allocation. Real-model numerics and GPU training were not tested; the PR remains unmerged.

title: Stable log-domain RBP and log-mean aggregation
contribution: LensKit provides recommender-system evaluation tools. Submitted LogRBP and log-mean aggregation to keep very small rank-biased precision values representable and distinguish log(mean RBP) from mean(log RBP). Added regression coverage for deep ranks, zero values and undefined results.
whyItMatters: Numerical underflow can erase distinctions in ranking evaluation. This is a historical backfill dated to the original submission, not a newly merged change or a complete resolution of the broader tuning request.

title: Audit merged-result summaries after error reruns
contribution: Claw-Eval evaluates agent tasks over repeated trials. Traced the --rerun-errors path: recovered task results are merged, while summary counters can still describe only the rerun subset. Documented a minimal three-task example and a fresh-versus-recovered regression contract.
whyItMatters: Recovery should preserve the denominator and statistics of the final result set. This public issue records a read-only source audit, not a full harness reproduction or an upstream code fix.

title: Audit cross-split discussion and target identities
contribution: PluRule evaluates rule-following in online discussions. Audited 13,371 released thread pairs, finding shared submission and target-comment IDs across splits; traced the pair-level split and optional RAG self-exclusion logic. Reported exact counts and found no direct role flips or answer-option mapping inconsistencies.
whyItMatters: Dataset independence depends on underlying discussion identity, not only row identity. No models were run, and the audit does not establish inflated published accuracy.

title: Report substring matching in step-attribution accuracy
contribution: TraceElephant evaluates agent failure attribution. Identified a string-containment check under which predicted step 10 can count as correct for reference step 1; documented the asymmetric counterexample and proposed an explicit single-step or multi-step parsing contract.
whyItMatters: An evaluator's matching rule can change which failure localizations count as correct. The report does not recompute published results or claim an accepted fix.

title: Audit reflection skills against executable tool schemas
contribution: Agent-Reflex releases reflection skills for agent training. Statically checked its 51-entry environment-skill catalog and found two environments whose skill text refers to unavailable tools: ten unresolved function references in total. Asked whether the catalog entries propagate into released training records.
whyItMatters: Textual guidance should match the tools an environment actually exposes. Training-data exposure and any effect on learning remain unverified; this is a catalog audit.

title: Check evaluation completeness before ledger comparisons
contribution: AutoMem's Loop 2 pipeline records evaluation progression for successive training iterations. Traced aggregation over available episode files without an expected-seed completeness gate, and illustrated how a missing low-scoring seed can change the reported mean.
whyItMatters: Partial and complete evaluations need explicit coverage before they can support model selection. The finding is source-level with an isolated scoring example, not an end-to-end pipeline failure.

title: Trace citation judgments into missing aggregation columns
contribution: Search Arena analyzes search-model responses and their citations. Compared emitted URL-level citation judgments with the final aggregation schema and reproduced a missing-column KeyError using a minimal DataFrame. Proposed reconstruction back to conversation rows and model sides.
whyItMatters: Intermediate evidence needs an explicit mapping to the unit being scored. This was an isolated schema check, not a reproduction of the Gemini annotation run or an audit of published scores.

title: Expose inconsistent denominators for empty student responses
contribution: Advisor-models evaluates advice through downstream student responses. Compared two review evaluators: one excludes empty responses from its accuracy denominator while another retains failures. Supplied an isolated comparison showing how response completion can alter apparent model ordering.
whyItMatters: Conditional accuracy and completion coverage answer different questions. The report asks for a consistent reporting contract without asserting an effect on the paper's results.

title: Audit incomplete validation in frontier admission
contribution: Meta-Harness evolves candidate harnesses and compares validation performance. Traced means computed from observed datasets and frontier recomputation after failed benchmark jobs; supplied an isolated example where incomplete coverage makes one candidate appear stronger.
whyItMatters: Selection should distinguish missing evaluation evidence from demonstrated improvement. This is a source audit and scoring check, not an end-to-end reproduction or a submitted implementation.

title: Reconstruct human outcome labels and inspect tie handling
contribution: Fara releases CUAVerifierBench annotations for computer-use verification. Reconstructed UV-informed judgments across 106 trajectories and 215 annotation records; majority voting with ties mapped to zero reproduces every released final label. Asked how third-reviewer adjudication is represented for the 17 tied trajectories.
whyItMatters: Reference-label provenance matters when evaluating verifiers. The reconstruction does not establish that the paper is wrong or that these judgments are UV-blind human references.

title: Probe task dependence in bootstrap-based evolution evidence
contribution: Beagle supports DarwinX agent evolution. Built a CPU-only synthetic sensitivity check around a vendored task-wise resampling helper, comparing independent-task resampling with family-level resampling when tasks within a family are perfectly correlated.
whyItMatters: Repeated-run noise and dependence across benchmark tasks are distinct sources of uncertainty. This deliberately extreme synthetic pilot does not establish a DarwinX failure or that this helper controls its current promotion path.

title: Trace RTI admission when the LLM post-check is unavailable
contribution: QQR's RTI pipeline checks corrective trajectories before downstream use. Identified a post-check fallback that returns ok=true when the LLM check is unavailable or unparseable, allowing otherwise eligible corrections to proceed to later gates. Proposed separating unavailable verification from an affirmative check.
whyItMatters: Other gates, including task success, still apply. This records a source-level observation and a proposed experiment; no invalid training admission or learning effect has been demonstrated.

title: Identify ordering sensitivity in semantic coverage precision
contribution: AACR-Bench evaluates code-review findings against reference comments. Derived a two-reference counterexample in the greedy novel-coverage calculation: permuting identical generated findings changes precision while recall stays fixed. Asked whether this ordering dependence is intentional.
whyItMatters: An evaluation contract can depend on presentation order even when semantic matches are unchanged. No dataset-level experiment or effect on published model comparisons is claimed.

title: Separate incorrect answers from reward-verification failures
contribution: Prefix-RL uses reward feedback for mathematical responses. Traced an offline reward path that returns the same numeric zero for incorrect answers and some parsing or verification exceptions, then proposed a separate diagnostic status without changing reward behavior.
whyItMatters: A zero reward alone cannot identify why evaluation failed. This is code inspection and a diagnostic proposal; training effects and the frequency of these paths were not measured.

title: Reproduce ShellOps and probe delayed consequences of an edit
contribution: A³ studies structured credit assignment for agent actions. Reproduced the ShellOps demo and used hand-designed continuations to compare an early workspace edit with no-edit and wrong-content controls: zero immediate reward need not mean no effect on later commands.
whyItMatters: This is a bounded environment-level counterfactual check, not a policy-generated rollout study or evidence that A³'s credit estimator improves learning.

title: Probe guidance-scheduler sensitivity with synthetic feedback
contribution: Agent-G² adapts guidance using historical rollout outcomes. Completed a CPU-only synthetic pilot at a pinned revision, checking trajectory deduplication, rollout-level success accounting and the Gaussian scheduler's response to persistent false-positive feedback.
whyItMatters: The pilot isolates scheduler mechanics and evidence units. It does not train a policy, establish an optimal guidance depth or measure downstream task performance.

title: Specify which memory revision a verification checked
contribution: Open Memory Protocol defines portable memory records and provenance. Supplied worked examples for known and unknown checked revisions, showing why a verification timestamp alone should not imply that the current memory body was checked.
whyItMatters: Revision identity prevents old verification from being read as support for changed content. A maintainer subsequently reported incorporating the rule and review case into the versioning draft; this is a review contribution, not authorship or merger of PR #13.

title: Prototype evidence gates for local preference-pair admission
contribution: Marin's BFCL recovery work retains local preference pairs. Built a standalone synthetic validator with 42 passing checks, distinguishing exact token-history and schema matching from verified pre-action environment equivalence; missing evidence stays unverified.
whyItMatters: Parser-level matching should not silently qualify examples for execution-level preference learning. The prototype does not modify Marin or rely on private BFCL traces; this backfill uses the original public update date.

title: Complete BBQ grouping and duplicate-definition reconciliation
contribution: The Inspect Evals uncertainty audit examines dependence between benchmark items. Audited BBQ's scenario structure, reconciled full-record versus prompt-content duplicate definitions, and verified exact group-membership agreement for both context and alternative grouping keys after a public correction.
whyItMatters: This completes the structural reconciliation, not an uncertainty-effect estimate. Per-item model scores were unavailable, so no empirical standard-error ratio or new inference result is claimed.

title: Locate dropped scorer-coverage fields in the GUI path
contribution: PyRIT evaluates AI red-teaming outcomes. Traced saved scorer metrics through the scenario progress projection to the GUI: scored-response and input-response counts existed upstream but were omitted before accuracy rendering. Proposed exposing coverage with conditional accuracy.
whyItMatters: Accuracy on scored responses can hide unevaluated inputs. This entry records the public diagnosis; it does not claim that the locally discussed patch is an upstream PR or merged fix.
